79894422.title: 2025 World Seniors Championship
79894422.extract:
The 2025 World Seniors Championship (officially the 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Championship) was a snooker tournament that took place from 7 to 11 May 2025 at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield, England, the seventh consecutive year that the tournament was held at the venue. Open to amateur players over 40 and professional players who were over 45 and also ranked outside the top 64 in the snooker world rankings, the event was the 16th edition of the World Seniors Championship, first held in 1991. Organised by the World Seniors Tour, the event was broadcast in the United Kingdom by Channel 5 and internationally by other broadcasters.
Igor Figueiredo was the defending champion, having defeated Ken Doherty 5‍–‍2 in the 2024 final, but he lost 2‍–‍4 to Wayne Townsend in the first round. Alfie Burden held leads of 4‍–‍1 and 7‍–‍2 against Aaron Canavan in the final and went on to win 8‍–‍4 to claim his first World Seniors title.
The tournament produced five century breaks, four of which were compiled by Dominic Dale, who also made the highest, a 131 in his semi-final match against Canavan. The final of the event was Michaela Tabb's last appearance as a traditional snooker referee, following a 24-year career during which she had refereed two World Championship finals.


== Overview ==

The 2025 World Seniors Championship was a snooker tournament that took place from 7 to 11 May 2025 at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield, England. The 16th edition of the World Seniors Championship, first played in 1991, it was held at the Crucible for the seventh consecutive year and sponsored by bookmaker JenningsBet. A World Seniors Tour event, the tournament was open to amateur players over 40 and professional players over 45, who also needed to be ranked outside the top 64 in the snooker world rankings. The event was broadcast in the United Kingdom on Channel 5 and by other broadcasters internationally. Igor Figueiredo was the defending champion, having defeated Ken Doherty 5‍–‍2 in the 2024 final. Four referees officiated: Mark Beale, Michaela Tabb, Rod Eaton, and Proletina Velichkova.


=== Participants ===
Figueiredo, as the defending champion, and was given the top seed. Other seeded players were Doherty, four-time winner of the event Jimmy White, Tony Drago and Tony Knowles. Joe Perry and Dominic Dale retired as professional players after their defeats in the qualifying stages of the 2025 World Championship, making them eligible to compete. Several players had to qualify. The winner of the 2018 edition, Aaron Canavan, as well as Andrew Norman, Gerard Greene and Townsend, qualified for the event during the so-called Race to the Crucible Series. Four more players qualified through various continental Seniors Championships: Craig Steadman won in Europe, Hassan Kerde in Asia-Pacific, Charl Jonck in Africa and Fabio Luersen in the Americas. Alfie Burden defeated Andy Lavin, Rodney Goggins, Stuart Watson and Matthew Ford to win the Golden Ticket tournament to qualify for the final stages.


=== Prize fund ===
The winner of the event received £20,000, with the runner-up earning £10,000.


== Summary ==


=== First round ===

The first round took place on 7 and 8 May, each match played as the best of 7 frames. Joe Perry made two breaks of 76 to take a 2‍–‍0 lead against Fabio Luersen and also compiled a 94 and a 59 to win 4‍–‍2. "I was a little bit nervous which I was pleased about, I didn't want to be flat and not care," Perry said. Craig Steadman recovered from 0‍–‍2 against Dominic Dale to tie the scores, but Dale then won the fifth frame and compiled a century break of 107 in the sixth to clinch a 4‍–‍2 victory. "To win a tournament at the Crucible would be fantastic—it's a special place to play," Dale said. Wayne Townsend won the first frame of the match against the defending champion, Igor Figueiredo, with a break of 53 and on the final black ball. Figueiredo replied with a half-century of his own and then took the lead at 2‍–‍1. Townsend won three frames on the spin, the last one again on the final black, to seal victory. "I'm on cloud nine. I was playing the world champion and I've knocked him out! There's no reason why I can't be the world champion and there is nobody here I can't beat," Townsend said after the match. Aaron Canavan manufactured breaks of 51, 89, 72 and 51 to defeat Andrew Norman 4‍–‍1. "If you enjoy it then the chances are that you will play better," Canavan conceded afterwards.
Alfie Burden faced Jimmy White, winner of the event in 2010, 2019, 2020 and 2023. Burden won the first two frames, but White produced a 82 break in the third to halve the deficit. Burden won the fourth frame on the re-spotted black and manufactured a 92 break in the fifth to advance into the quarter-finals. Burden commented after the match that he had first practiced with White when he was 15 years old and that he was sure White would want him to go on to win the tournament now: "We've had this amazing friendship for many years and I don't get any pleasure in beating Jimmy [White] but I was focused on winning and I had to blank out who I was playing." Ken Doherty took a 2‍–‍0 lead against Charl Jonck, but Jonck went on to win four consecutive frames, featuring breaks of 64 and 63, to win the match. "That was surreal. It was the lifelong ambition becoming a reality," Jonck said. Tony Drago compiled a 75 break in the first frame of his duel with Gerard Greene. The match went into a decider, which Drago won aided by a break of 68. Hassan Kerde whitewashed Tony Knowles, making breaks of 53, 62, 66 and 59 in the process. "I'm over the moon. I've watched the Crucible for the last 20 years and to just come and watch a match would have been awesome," Kerde said afterwards.


=== Quarter-finals ===
The quarter-finals took place on 9 May, each match played as the best of 7 frames. Dale compiled breaks of 97, 99 and 128 as he beat Perry 4‍–‍1. "I've been practicing hard here and I've found some form. I was confident going into the match," Dale commented. In his match against Burden, Drago won the first frame and then took two consecutive frames on the re-spotted black to edge 3‍–‍0 in front. Burden won four on the spin, featuring breaks of 53 and 51, to advance into the semi-finals.
Kerde and Jonck shared the first four frames, but Kerde then took two, one of them with a break of 85, to win the match. "I'm the first person to come from Australia and reach the semi-finals of the World Seniors Snooker Championship and hopefully I can do the country proud," Kerde said. Canavan took a 3‍–‍1 lead against Townsend, who compiled an 85 break in the fifth frame to halve the deficit. Canavan went on to take the following frame and seal victory with a 4‍–‍2 result.


=== Semi-finals ===
The semi-finals took place on 10 May, both matches played as the best of 11 frames. Burden produced breaks of 57 and 65 as he took a 4‍–‍0 lead against Kerde. Kerde replied by winning two consecutive frames and halving the deficit, but Burden made a break of 97 to go 5‍–‍2 in front and won the following frame to clinch victory. "It was a tough game but I was pleased with the way I played and it stands me in good stead for the final," Burden said afterwards.
Canavan and Dale shared the first four frames of their semi-final. Dale then made back-to-back century breaks, of 109 and 131, and won another frame to go within one of victory at 5‍–‍2. Canavan, however, won four consecutive frames, including the decider, to book a place in the final. "It was tough. After last night, I was really tired but I gave myself a good talking to in the dressing room and came out fighting," Canavan confessed.


=== Final ===

On 11 May, Burden and Canavan contested the best-of-15-frame final, which was divided into three mini-sessions of five frames each. Both players were competing in a World Seniors final for the second time, Canavan having won the title in 2018 and Burden having been runner-up in 2023. The first five-frame mini-session was refereed by Michaela Tabb, who retired from traditional snooker refereeing after the tournament, following a 24-year career that had included two World Championship finals. Canavan won the opening frame, but Burden then won four consecutive frames with breaks including 74 and 54 as he moved 4–1 ahead. Proletina Velichkova refereed the remainder of the final.
Canavan won the first frame of the second mini-session, but Burden took three consecutive frames with breaks of 65, 109, and 80. Canavan won the 8th frame to leave Burden leading 7–3. The third and final mini-session lasted two frames, as Canavan won frame 11 but Burden made a 76 break in the 12th to secure an 8–4 victory and win his first World Seniors title. He said afterwards: "I'm absolutely delighted. I thought I played well in the final. It's been a massive journey with so many ups and downs. I think it's been well documented that I think I've underachieved in my career but you've got to enjoy this moment."

Four more players qualified through various continental Seniors Championships: [[Craig Steadman]] won in Europe, Hassan Kerde in Asia-Pacific, Charl Jonck in Africa and Fabio Luersen in the Americas.<ref name="WSTlineup">{{cite web|title=Line-Up Confirmed for 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship|url=https://seniorssnooker.com/line-up-confirmed-for-2025-jenningsbet-world-seniors-snooker-championship/|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=8 April 2025|access-date=7 May 2025|archive-date=8 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250408102309/https://seniorssnooker.com/line-up-confirmed-for-2025-jenningsbet-world-seniors-snooker-championship/|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Alfie Burden]] defeated Andy Lavin, [[Rodney Goggins]], Stuart Watson and Matthew Ford to win the Golden Ticket tournament to qualify for the final stages.<ref name="WSTBurden">{{cite web|title=Alfie Burden Secures Crucible Spot|url=https://seniorssnooker.com/alfie-burden-secures-crucible-spot/|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=22 April 2025|access-date=7 May 2025|archive-date=22 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250422224910/https://seniorssnooker.com/alfie-burden-secures-crucible-spot/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Prize fund ===
The winner of the event received £20,000, with the runner-up earning £10,000.<ref name="snookerorg2025"/>

==Summary==
===First round===
{{Multiple image |direction=horizontal |image2=Joe Perry at Snooker German Masters (DerHexer) 2013-01-31 01.jpg |image1=Dominic Dale PHC 2016-2.jpg |total_width=275 |alt2=photo of Joe Perry |alt1=photo of Dominic Dale |footer=[[Dominic Dale]] ''(pictured left in 2016)'' and [[Joe Perry (snooker player)|Joe Perry]] ''(pictured right in 2013)'' both made their debut in the [[World Seniors Championship]] after  retiring from professional competition.}}

The first round took place on 7 and 8 May, each match played as the best of 7 {{cuegloss|frame|frames}}.<ref name="wstorder"/><ref name="snookerorg2025"/> [[Joe Perry (snooker player)|Joe Perry]] made two breaks of 76 to take a 2{{nbnd}}0 lead against Fabio Luersen and also compiled a 94 and a 59 to win 4{{nbnd}}2.<ref>{{cite web|title=Match Sheet: Last 16 - Joe Perry vs Fabio Luersen|url=https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e3d9-73e4-92c4-e4ef3969a570/sheet|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=7 May 2025|access-date=7 May 2025|archive-date=7 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250507143546/https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e3d9-73e4-92c4-e4ef3969a570/sheet|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Townsendstuns">{{cite web|title=Townsend Stuns Defending Champion to Join Perry, Dale and Canavan in the Quarters|url=https://seniorssnooker.com/townsend-stuns-defending-champion-to-join-perry-dale-and-canavan-in-the-quarters/|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=8 May 2025|access-date=8 May 2025}}</ref> "I was a little bit nervous which I was pleased about, I didn't want to be flat and not care," Perry said. [[Craig Steadman]] recovered from 0{{nbnd}}2 against [[Dominic Dale]] to tie the scores, but Dale then won the fifth frame and compiled a [[century break]] of 107 in the sixth to clinch a 4{{nbnd}}2 victory.<ref name="Townsendstuns"/><ref>{{cite web|title=Match Sheet: Last 16 - Dominic Dale vs Craig Steadman|url=https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e3ac-7071-a94f-55f3adda460d/sheet|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=8 May 2025|access-date=8 May 2025|archive-date=7 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250507162638/https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e3ac-7071-a94f-55f3adda460d/sheet|url-status=live}}</ref> "To win a tournament at the Crucible would be fantastic—it's a special place to play," Dale said. Wayne Townsend won the first frame of the match against the defending champion, [[Igor Figueiredo]], with a break of 53 and on the final {{cuegloss|black ball}}. Figueiredo replied with a half-century of his own and then took the lead at 2{{nbnd}}1. Townsend won three frames on the spin, the last one again on the final black, to seal victory.<ref name="FigueiredoTownsend">{{cite web|title=Match Sheet: Last 16 - Igor Figueiredo vs Wayne Townsend|url=https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e366-7150-bd85-b0268123100b/sheet|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=8 May 2025|access-date=8 May 2025|archive-date=8 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250508002737/https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e366-7150-bd85-b0268123100b/sheet|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Townsendstuns"/> "I'm on cloud nine. I was playing the world champion and I've knocked him out! There's no reason why I can't be the world champion and there is nobody here I can't beat," Townsend said after the match.<ref name="Townsendstuns"/> [[Aaron Canavan]] manufactured breaks of 51, 89, 72 and 51 to defeat [[Andrew Norman (snooker player)|Andrew Norman]] 4{{nbnd}}1.<ref>{{cite web|title=Match Sheet: Last 16 - Aaron Canavan vs Andrew Norman|url=https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e389-7373-9fd7-9afde4281b0c/sheet|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=8 May 2025|access-date=8 May 2025|archive-date=8 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250508090730/https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e389-7373-9fd7-9afde4281b0c/sheet|url-status=live}}</ref> "If you enjoy it then the chances are that you will play better," Canavan conceded afterwards.<ref name="Townsendstuns"/>

[[Alfie Burden]] faced [[Jimmy White]], winner of the event in [[2010 World Seniors Championship|2010]], [[2019 World Seniors Championship|2019]], [[2020 World Seniors Championship|2020]] and [[2023 World Seniors Championship|2023]].<ref name="WSTlineup"/> Burden won the first two frames, but White produced a 82 break in the third to halve the deficit. Burden won the fourth frame on the {{cuegloss|re-spotted black}} and manufactured a 92 break in the fifth to advance into the quarter-finals.<ref name="WhiteBurden">{{cite web|title=Match Sheet: Last 16 - Jimmy White vs Alfie Burden|url=https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e400-73cd-9218-b48f006dd374/sheet|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=8 May 2025|access-date=8 May 2025}}</ref><ref name="WDdowned">{{cite web|title=White and Doherty Downed on Day of Upsets at the Crucible|url=https://seniorssnooker.com/white-and-doherty-downed-on-day-of-upsets-at-the-crucible/|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=9 May 2025|access-date=9 May 2025}}</ref> Burden commented after the match that he had first practiced with White when he was 15 years old and that he was sure White would want him to go on to win the tournament now: "We've had this amazing friendship for many years and I don't get any pleasure in beating Jimmy [White] but I was focused on winning and I had to blank out who I was playing."<ref name="WDdowned"/> [[Ken Doherty]] took a 2{{nbnd}}0 lead against Charl Jonck, but Jonck went on to win four consecutive frames, featuring breaks of 64 and 63, to win the match.<ref>{{cite web|title=Match Sheet: Last 16 - Ken Doherty vs Charl Jonck|url=https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e466-70ca-a784-89f770426701/sheet|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=8 May 2025|access-date=9 May 2025|archive-date=9 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250509021959/https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e466-70ca-a784-89f770426701/sheet|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="WDdowned"/> "That was surreal. It was the lifelong ambition becoming a reality," Jonck said.<ref name="WDdowned"/> [[Tony Drago]] compiled a 75 break in the first frame of his duel with [[Gerard Greene]]. The match went into a {{cuegloss|deciding frame|decider}}, which Drago won aided by a break of 68.<ref name="DragoGreene">{{cite web|title=Match Sheet: Last 16 - Tony Drago vs Gerard Greene|url=https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e423-71c1-9ce9-259fbfcc6f5d/sheet|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=8 May 2025|access-date=9 May 2025}}</ref><ref name="WDdowned"/> Hassan Kerde [[Whitewash (sport)|whitewashed]] [[Tony Knowles (snooker player)|Tony Knowles]], making breaks of 53, 62, 66 and 59 in the process.<ref>{{cite web|title=Match Sheet: Last 16 - Tony Knowles vs Hassan Kerde|url=https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e443-726f-80c8-6c3386435cbe/sheet|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=8 May 2025|access-date=9 May 2025}}</ref><ref name="WDdowned"/> "I'm over the moon. I've watched the Crucible for the last 20 years and to just come and watch a match would have been awesome," Kerde said afterwards.<ref name="WDdowned"/>

===Quarter-finals===
The quarter-finals took place on 9 May, each match played as the best of 7 frames.<ref name="wstorder"/><ref name="snookerorg2025"/> Dale compiled breaks of 97, 99 and 128 as he beat Perry 4{{nbnd}}1.<ref>{{cite web|title=Match Sheet: Quarter-final - Joe Perry vs Dominic Dale|url=https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e2eb-710b-b6f9-0783be6688b6/sheet|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=9 May 2025|access-date=9 May 2025|archive-date=9 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250509135930/https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e2eb-710b-b6f9-0783be6688b6/sheet|url-status=live}}</ref> "I've been practicing hard here and I've found some form. I was confident going into the match," Dale commented.<ref name="quarters">{{cite web|title=Dale, Burden, Kerde and Canavan Into the Semi-Finals|url=https://seniorssnooker.com/dale-burden-kerde-and-canavan-into-the-semi-finals/|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=10 May 2025|access-date=12 May 2025}}</ref> In his match against Burden, Drago won the first frame and then took two consecutive frames on the re-spotted black to edge 3{{nbnd}}0 in front. Burden won four on the spin, featuring breaks of 53 and 51, to advance into the semi-finals.<ref name="DragoBurden">{{cite web|title=Match Sheet: Last 16 - Tony Drago vs Alfie Burden|url=https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e314-706b-8971-5c83cfe9cdad/sheet|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=9 May 2025|access-date=12 May 2025}}</ref><ref name="quarters"/>

Kerde and Jonck shared the first four frames, but Kerde then took two, one of them with a break of 85, to win the match.<ref>{{cite web|title=Match Sheet: Last 16 - Hassan Kerde vs Charl Jonck|url=https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e341-70ca-b949-46d463aab6b3/sheet|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=9 May 2025|access-date=12 May 2025}}</ref> "I'm the first person to come from Australia and reach the semi-finals of the World Seniors Snooker Championship and hopefully I can do the country proud," Kerde said.<ref name="quarters"/> Canavan took a 3{{nbnd}}1 lead against Townsend, who compiled an 85 break in the fifth frame to halve the deficit. Canavan went on to take the following frame and seal victory with a 4{{nbnd}}2 result.<ref name="CanavanTownsend">{{cite web|title=Match Sheet: Last 16 - Aaron Canavan vs Wayne Townsend|url=https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e2cd-72c9-ae27-1daefbef4c18/sheet|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=9 May 2025|access-date=12 May 2025}}</ref>

===Semi-finals===
The semi-finals took place on 10 May, both matches played as the best of 11 frames.<ref name="wstorder"/><ref name="snookerorg2025"/> Burden produced breaks of 57 and 65 as he took a 4{{nbnd}}0 lead against Kerde. Kerde replied by winning two consecutive frames and halving the deficit, but Burden made a break of 97 to go 5{{nbnd}}2 in front and won the following frame to clinch victory.<ref name="BurdenKerde">{{cite web|title=Match Sheet: Semi-final - Alfie Burden vs Hassan Kerde|url=https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e2a4-7251-8924-9d86a2e1f689/sheet|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=10 May 2025|access-date=12 May 2025}}</ref><ref name="semis">{{cite web|title=Burden and Canavan Set Up World Final Meeting|url=https://seniorssnooker.com/burden-and-canavan-set-up-world-final-meeting/|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=11 May 2025|access-date=12 May 2025}}</ref> "It was a tough game but I was pleased with the way I played and it stands me in good stead for the final," Burden said afterwards.<ref name="BurdenKerde"/>

Canavan and Dale shared the first four frames of their semi-final. Dale then made back-to-back century breaks, of 109 and 131, and won another frame to go within one of victory at 5{{nbnd}}2. Canavan, however, won four consecutive frames, including the decider, to book a place in the final.<ref name="CanavanDale">{{cite web|title=Match Sheet: Semi-final - Aaron Canavan vs Dominic Dale|url=https://snookerscores.net/scoreboard/match/01963902-e287-7382-bfbd-ef84628c9e8d/sheet|work=[[World Seniors Tour]]|date=10 May 2025|access-date=12 May 2025}}</ref><ref name="semis"/> "It was tough. After last night, I was really tired but I gave myself a good talking to in the dressing room and came out fighting," Canavan confessed.<ref name="semis"/>

===Final===
[[File:Alfie Burden and Thorsten Müller at Snooker German Masters (DerHexer) 2015-02-05 01.jpg|thumb|left|upright=0.8|alt=Alfie Burden playing a shot|[[Alfie Burden]] ''(pictured in 2015)'' defeated [[Aaron Canavan]] 8{{nbnd}}4 in the final to claim his first [[World Seniors Championship]] title.]]

On 11 May, Burden and Canavan contested the best-of-15-frame final, which was divided into three mini-sessions of five frames each.<ref name="wstorder"/><ref name="snookerorg2025"/><ref name="Burden.Win">{{cite web |last=Watterson |first=Ryan |date=12 May 2025 |title=Alfie Burden wins 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship |url=https://seniorssnooker.com/alfie-burden-wins-2025-jenningsbet-world-seniors-snooker-championship/ |access-date=12 May 2025 |website=[[World Seniors Tour]]}}</ref> Both players were competing in a World Seniors final for the second time, Canavan having won the title in [[2018 World Seniors Championship|2018]] and Burden having been runner-up in [[2023 World Seniors Championship|2023]]. The first five-frame mini-session was refereed by [[Michaela Tabb]], who retired from traditional snooker refereeing after the tournament, following a 24-year career that had included two [[World Snooker Championship|World Championship]] finals.<ref name="Burden.Win" /><ref>{{Cite web|date=19 March 2015 |title=Michaela Tabb, snooker’s highest-profile female referee, leaves circuit |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2015/mar/19/michaela-tab-snooker-referee-leaves|access-date=2025-10-13 |website=The Guardian |language=en}}</ref> Canavan won the opening frame, but Burden then won four consecutive frames with breaks including 74 and 54 as he moved 4–1 ahead.<ref name="Burden.Win" /> Proletina Velichkova refereed the remainder of the final.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.gazettelive.co.uk/sport/world-snooker-championship-final-referee-31628967|title=World Snooker Championship final referee explains quits decision with classy message|work=Gazette Live|first=Stuart|last=Jamieson|first2=Kasra|last2=Moradi|access-date=13 October 2025|date=13 May 2025}}</ref>

Canavan won the first frame of the second mini-session, but Burden took three consecutive frames with breaks of 65, 109, and 80. Canavan won the 8th frame to leave Burden leading 7–3. The third and final mini-session lasted two frames, as Canavan won frame 11 but Burden made a 76 break in the 12th to secure an 8–4 victory and win his first World Seniors title. He said afterwards: "I'm absolutely delighted. I thought I played well in the final. It's been a massive journey with so many ups and downs. I think it's been well documented that I think I've underachieved in my career but you've got to enjoy this moment."<ref name="Burden.Win" />
